explanation: Compute existing all-pairs shortest paths with Floyd–Warshall. For each candidate edge, test both directions of using it once for every city pair and sum the savings. Replace the best only for a strict improvement, preserving the first proposal on ties.
timeComplexity: O(h+n³+p·n²): initialize h roads, run three nested Floyd–Warshall loops, then score each of p proposals on O(n²) city pairs.
spaceComplexity: O(n²) for the all-pairs distance matrix; proposal scoring keeps only running savings and the best proposal.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Floyd–Warshall establishes the shortest existing distance between every pair. Any shortest path improved by one new nonnegative undirected edge can use that edge at most once, in either direction; testing those two possibilities therefore finds its new distance. Summing pair savings compares proposals correctly, and updating only on a strict improvement preserves the first proposal on ties.
walkthrough: With highways (0,1,8),(1,2,8), existing pair distances sum to 8+8+16=32. Adding (0,2,3) reduces the sum to 8+8+3=19, saving 13. Adding (0,1,4) gives 4+8+12=24, saving 8. Choose proposal (0,2,3).
edgeCases: A proposal may duplicate an existing road with a smaller distance.
Equal total savings choose the earliest proposal.
Long arithmetic stores path distances and total savings.
